packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET 08 - FIRST READING (image-only, unverified)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- No proposed identification of the work or author reached me in my context. My task brief named only the packet directory.
- Two things in the materials hint at provenance, not at the work. (a) The packet path contains "stams3". (b) Modern pencil labels are photographed on the leaves: "Stams, STA, Frg. 70_1r", "..._2r", "..._2v", "..._3r", "..._3v". There are also blue oval stickers reading "IV. 46", "IV. 45" and "IV. 44", and a later ink number "1913"(?) on image-017. I record these as observed and did not use them for any reading.
- I did nothing beyond the rules: I listed this packet directory and read pixel sizes with sips to tell overviews from tiles, read PROMPT.md, and viewed all 38 images. I opened no other directory, did no web search and did not read packet.json.
- All 38 images loaded.

IMAGE MAP (from sizes and content)
- Face A: overview image-001; tiles image-002..017 (4 x 4 grid). The overview shows two bifolia, one above the other. The tiles cover both.
- Face B: overview image-018; tiles image-019..024 (3 x 2). These tiles cover ONLY the lower bifolium. The upper bifolium of face B appears only in the reduced overview.
- Face C: overview image-025; tiles image-026..031. One damaged bifolium with an irregular "house" outline.
- Face D: overview image-032; tiles image-033..038. The same fragment from the other side, heavily stained.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Parchment bifolia, single column per page, ruled. Gothic textualis in brown/black ink with red rubrics.
- Rubrics observed: "Lc. vi." / "Lc. vii." / "Lc. viii." / "Lectio. ii." (lesson numbers); "R" and "V" (responsory/versicle signs); "ad .iii. a." / "ad .ix. a." (hour antiphons?); "Cap." (capitulum?); "coll." / "collecta"; "Inv." (invitatory?); "In sec(un)dis v(e)s(peris)"; "Ant." ; "ps.".
- Pen-flourished initials alternate red and blue, with filigree in the contrasting colour (red or blue-grey) running into the margin. Smaller one-line capitals are touched in red.
- Face A, upper-right page: a later hand has written large cursive pen trials over the text in black ink, perhaps a name like "Ambros..." and letters such as "Z", "9", "8". The leaf also has many holes.
- Face C/D: a later hand has also added large black flourishes over the lower lines of the left column on face C.
- Tentative interpretation (not an identification): liturgical office text, i.e. lessons alternating with responsories, chapters, collects and antiphons.

SELECTED SPANS AND WHAT REMAINS UNREAD
- Read: Face B lower-right page (very legible); Face C left page and right page (legible); Face D right page (partly); Face D left page lower lines; Face A lower-right page, lesson ii; Face A upper-left page, top lines (faded).
- Mostly unread: Face A upper-right page (overwritten, holed, faded) and Face A lower-left page (badly faded; rubrics only). Face B lower-left page has been largely stripped away and only line-ends survive. Face B upper bifolium was read only from the reduced overview, so a native-resolution tile set for it is requested. The upper halves of Face D are badly stained.

CONVENTIONS: ( ) = expansion; ? after a word = uncertain; [illegible] = not readable by me; / = line break where lines run on. Line numbers count from the top of the named image, using visible text lines only.

======================================================================
FACE B, LOWER BIFOLIUM, RIGHT PAGE (tiles image-020, -021, -023, -024)
Clearest text in the packet. Rows 1-17 below are text lines in image-021 (left part continued in image-020).
image-021 L1  [rec]u(m)bentib(us) [ (upper right torn away / repaired) ]
image-021 L2  [ei]us (et) dabo tibi. Et iura[uit?]
image-021 L3  [pet]ieris dabo tibi licet dimid[ium?]   (image-020: "petieris dabo ti[bi]")
image-021 L4  [image-020: "mei."] Que cu(m) exisset dixit matri sue.
image-021 L5  [image-020: "petam."] At illa dixit. Caput iohannis bapte(ste).
image-021 L6  [image-020: "Cu(m)q(ue) introisset"] statim cu(m) festinatione
image-021 L7  [image-020: "ad rege(m)"] petiuit dicens. Volo ut p(ro)tinus
image-021 L8  [image-020: "des michi"] in disco cap(ut) iohannis bapte(ste). Et
image-021 L9  [image-020: "contristatus"] e(st) rex p(ro)p(ter) ius iurandu(m) et
image-021 L10 [image-020: "p(ro)p(ter)"] simul recu(m)bentes. noluit [illegible, stain] [con]tristari?   (end of line damaged)
image-021 L11 [image-020: "s(ed)"] misso spiculatore p(re)cepit [illegible, stain] [affer]ri? capu(t)
image-021 L12 [image-020: "eius"] in disco. Et decollauit eu(m) in carcere
image-021 L13 [image-020: "(et)"] attulit cap(ut) eius in disco. (et) dedit illud
image-021 L14 [image-020: "puelle."] (et) puella dedit matri sue. Quo
image-021 L15 [image-020: "audito"] discipuli eius uenerunt (et) tulerunt
image-021 L16 [image-020: "corpus"] ei(us) (et) posuerunt illud i(n) monumento.
image-021 L17 [image-020: "Am(en)?" or "...m."] coll(ecta). Beati iohannis bapte(ste). Inv(itatorium)? a(ntiphona). Herodes
image-024 L5  [image-023: "e(n)i(m)"] tenuit (et) ligauit iohe(m) (et) posuit eu(m) i(n) carcere(m)
image-024 L6  [image-023: "p(ro)p(ter)"] herodiade(m). Cap(itulum). Sci(enti)? indiuia?/ "Sci indiba" [reading uncertain]. R. Posuisti? d[omine]?
image-024 L7  [image-023: "V. Iustus"] ger(minabit)? ad .iii. a(ntiphona). Misso herodes spicula-
image-024 L8  [image-023: "tore"] p(re)cepit amputari cap(ut) ioh(ann)is i(n) carcere. q(uo)d audi-
image-024 L9  [image-023: "to"] discipuli eius uenerunt (et) tulerunt corp(us) ei(us) (et) po-
image-024 L10 [image-023: "suerunt"] illud i(n) monumento. ad .vi. a(ntiphona). Puelle sal[tanti?]
- Below image-024 L10: blank ruled lower margin; pencil "Stams, STA, Frg. 70_2v".
- Notes: in L6 "Cap." is in red; the word after it looks like "Sci" plus "indiba" (or "indiuia" / "in diebus"?). I leave it unresolved. In L7 "ad .iii. a." is red, written with a superscript "a".

======================================================================
FACE B, LOWER BIFOLIUM, LEFT PAGE (image-019, -020, -023, -022)
- Most of the page surface has been lost or stripped (pale, layered parchment). Only a narrow strip of line-ends survives next to the gutter.
image-020 line-ends from top: "...[ill] ierunt?" / "...anis? tem?" / [blank?] / "...lis legis" / "...[ill] non si?" / "...ti? p(re)cursor" / "...cer(e)? me" / "...b(e)ata? co" / "...l(a)uit? ea(m)?" / "...[ill] uir?" / red "Lc. iii."? (rubric "Lc. [ii/iii]") / "...ta. d(omi)n(u)m?" / "...[ill]" / "...[ill] q(uo)d" / "...q(ui)d? di" / "...es baptista" / "...[ill] tulerat?"
image-023 continues: "...eni? tenuit" / "...[ill] i(n) p(re)?" + red "R"? / red "Lc. v." / "...[ill]" / "...cursor?" / "...[ill] onios?" / "...[ill]"
- Image-022 shows the lower-left part of this page: no text survives there, only traces of red filigree in the left margin.

======================================================================
FACE B, UPPER BIFOLIUM (overview image-018 ONLY; no tiles; low confidence)
Left page (overview only):
 - Top lines: "...[ill] regnabit? p(o)st me ... / ...uos? ...[ill] ... / ...[ill] igno?..."; then red rubric "Dnica? viii.? Lc. j." (uncertain).
 - Blue/red initial I: "In diebus illis. congregati? sunt ..." [rest illegible at this resolution]
 - Initial (T?), then initial S, then initial S again with blue-grey filigree: "Siquide(m)? cherubin? ... alas / sup(er) loc(um) arche? ..."
 - Red rubrics "Lc. ii." and "Lc. iii." are visible in the line-ends. Catchword(?) "...uecces" or similar centred in the lower margin.
Right page (overview only):
 - "R. Montes gelboe ... nec ros nec / pluuia? ueniant sup(er) uos? ... qui? ..." (approximate)
 - Red initial A ("A[...]"), with red "Lc. vi." at the end of the preceding line.
 - Nearly all of the rest is unreadable at overview resolution.
 -> REQUEST: native-resolution tiles of the upper bifolium of face B (overview image-018, top half).

======================================================================
FACE C (overview image-025; tiles image-026..031)
Left page, image-026 (left half) + image-027 (right half). Line 1 is the first visible text line.
L1  [image-026] ...[ill]natibus modul(is) dulcisona [image-027] ...modul(is) dulcisona cant[ica?]
L2  ...na? (con)sonant? / "...na ins[...]ant?" R. Corde (et) a(n)i(m)o (christ)o canam(us) gl(ori)-
L3  am. In hac sacra sollempnitate p(re)celse genitricis
L4  dei marie. V. Omnis parit(er)? (con)gregata? d(e)o? collaudem(us).
L5  [Red A with filigree] Audite ergo. que(m)admodu(m)   red: Lc. vii.  In
L6  tympanistria n(ost)ra cantauit. Au-?/"Ait"?   (image-027 ends with "Ait"? or "Au-")
L7  e(m). Magnificat a(n)i(m)a mea d(omi)n(u)m. Et exul-
L8  tauit sp(iritu)s meus in deo salutari meo. O?/C?
L9  b(ea)ta? [ill: struck by later flourish] ...(con)fera? omne captiuu(m) [ill: "mirum"?]   (image-027: "...omne captiuu(m) mun[...]")
L10 de(n)i?catur assensu(m)? / "...tur assensu(m)." Te d(omi)na? mu(n)dus i(n)?...   (image-029/-030: "assensu. Te dna mudus? iu?" ; reading of "mu(n)dus" uncertain)
L11 fidei obsides fecit? / "fidei obside(m) fecit." Noli morari uirgo
L12 nuncio festinanti responde u(er)bu(m) (et) suscipe?   (image-030: "respo(n)de u(er)bu(m) (et) susci-")
L13 pe filiu(m). Da fide(m) (con)senti? u(ir)tute(m)? / "Da fide(m) (con)senti(ens)? ... uirtuti?". R. Regali
L14 ex progenie maria exorta refulget. Cui(us) p(re)cib(us)
L15 nos adiuuari me(n)te (et) sp(irit)u deuotissime poscim(us). V.
L16 C[orde] (et) a(n)i(m)o (christ)o canam(us) gl(ori)am in hac sacra sol-
L17 lempnitate genitricis dei marie. Cui(us). red: Lc. viii.
